demand.reason: Global neodymium consumption is estimated between 40,000–60,000 tons of oxide-equivalent per year, placing it firmly within the moderate-demand band of 10,000–100,000 tons.

growth.reason: Demand is driven by NdFeB permanent magnets for EV traction motors and direct-drive wind turbines. Independent market analyses project NdFeB magnet demand growth at roughly 6.8–8.5% CAGR, securely placing it in the moderate-growth band (6–12% CAGR).

supplier_concentration.reason:
Mining: China produces approximately 69% of global rare-earth-oxide output, placing primary extraction in the 65–85% band (Score 4).


Refining: The separation of neodymium into oxide and metal is overwhelmingly concentrated in China, holding a 90–95% market share that exceeds the 85% threshold (Score 5).

reserves.reason:
Time-frame: Global rare-earth reserves exceed 85,000,000 tons. Against annual demand, the embedded neodymium fraction represents centuries of supply, which is effectively limitless (>100 years).


Diversification: Total global reserves yield a calculated HHI of approximately 0.34, with China holding roughly 51.8% of the reserve base. This places the geographic endowment in the moderately-concentrated band.

end_use.reason:
Electrification & Transport (+1.0): functions as the primary magnetic material in >90% of EV traction motors. Energy Generation & Grid (+1.5): essential for large-mass NdFeB generators in direct-drive wind turbines. Defense & National Security (+1.5): critical for precision-guided munitions, drones, and naval propulsion. Advanced Semiconductors & Computing (+1.0): utilized in hard-disk-drive voice-coil motors. Healthcare & Biomedical (+1.0): incorporated into MRI machines and Nd:YAG surgical lasers.


Sector presence scores total 6.0 across 5 qualifying sectors. The breadth bonus adds +2.0, yielding a composite score of 8.0.

substitutability_recyclability.reason:
Substitutability: Ferrite magnets or rare-earth-free motor architectures carry significant size, weight, and efficiency penalties. No commercially proven drop-in material substitute exists for high-energy-density NdFeB magnets at scale, requiring fundamental redesigns (Score 4).


Recyclability: Neodymium magnets are embedded in highly dispersed hardware. End-of-life recovery remains below 5% of supply due to severe economic and logistical barriers, tracking strictly in the negligible (<5%) recycling tier.

extraction_refining.reason: Neodymium extraction demands multi-stage counter-current solvent-extraction cascades to separate it from near-identical lanthanides, followed by molten-salt electrolysis. This is integrated with radioactive thorium/uranium byproduct management, classifying it as a nation-state level capability.

upcoming_projects.reason: The project pipeline is adequate. Neodymium serves as the primary economic anchor for expanding facilities like MP Materials (US) and Lynas (Australia/Malaysia), which have secured offtakes and are capable of adding 10–20% to non-Chinese supply over 3–5 years.

india_position.reason:
Import Dependence: IREL produces minor volumes of NdPr oxalate from monazite. However, this satisfies <20% of the rapidly growing domestic EV and wind sector demand, leaving India highly import-dependent within the marginal domestic production band.


Strategic Posture: Neodymium is heavily targeted by India's National Critical Mineral Mission and the ₹7,280 crore scheme for sintered rare earth permanent magnets (6,000 t/yr, approved November 2025; 20 bids in August 2026). This signifies concrete plans in motion, with domestic refining and magnet capacity under construction with a 3–7 year timeline.

price_volatility.reason: Neodymium prices swung from a trough of $56/kg to a peak of $134/kg over the evaluated window. This 139% increase from trough-to-peak vastly exceeds the 100% threshold, demonstrating high volatility driven by cyclical magnet demand shocks.

capability.name: Neodymium
capability.next_move: Oxide to metal to magnet at scale (the magnet scheme), plus magnet-scrap recycling.
capability.what_india_has: IREL's separation (Odisha, Kerala) and Toyotsu's Vizag plant; mini metal plants (La, Ce, Nd) at Bhopal; BARC and DMRL magnet know-how; 20 bidders for the integrated oxide-to-magnet scheme; IREL plans to buy 1,000 t of Nd/NdPr oxide.
capability.cost: Rs 7,280 crore of incentives for 6,000 t/yr; a 2,000 t/yr magnet plant costs over EUR 100 m (Neo, Estonia) (#2, #3).

stages.india: 2.9 kt of REO in 2025; 13 Mt of monazite plus ~1.2 Mt of REO in hard rock.
IREL made ~40 t of Nd in FY25 (target 500 t in FY27); Toyotsu (Vizag) separates La, Ce, Pr, Nd.

stages.world: NdPr metal and magnets: China 94% of sintered magnets.
stages.india: Mini Nd-metal plant at Bhopal; Rs 7,280 crore magnet scheme (6,000 t/yr; 20 bids).

strategyList.name: Rare-earth separation
strategyList.what: Hundreds of solvent-extraction stages split chemically near-identical rare earths into pure oxides.
strategyList.outside_china: China ~91%. Malaysia (Lynas, heavy REEs since 2025); France (Caremag, 2026); Australia (Iluka, being built).
strategyList.cost: Iluka Eneabba (Australia): A$1.7-1.8 bn for ~17.5 kt/yr of REO, incl. up to ~5.5 kt NdPr and ~0.75 kt Dy/Tb. Caremag (France): EUR 216 m, incl. ~600 t/yr of Dy/Tb oxides.
strategyList.india_base: IREL (light REEs, commercial; heavy REEs at pilot scale); Toyotsu (Vizag); solvent-extraction skills in pharma and chemical firms.

strategyList.name: Rare-earth metal making (metallisation)
strategyList.what: Turning oxides into metal: molten-salt electrolysis for Nd and Pr; calcium reduction of fluorides for Dy, Tb and Gd. The step before alloys and magnets.
strategyList.outside_china: Little capacity outside China; exact shares are not published.
strategyList.cost: India's magnet scheme funds oxide to metal to alloy to magnet: Rs 7,280 crore (Rs 6,450 crore sales incentives + Rs 750 crore capital subsidy) for 6,000 t/yr.
strategyList.india_base: Mini plants for La, Ce and Nd metal at the Bhopal theme park; BARC and DMRL know-how; scheme bidders must include this step.
strategyList.gap: Commercial electrolysis cells; fluoride chemistry for heavy-REE metals.

strategyList.name: Permanent magnet making
strategyList.what: Alloying, strip casting, jet milling, pressing, sintering and coating (NdFeB); reduction-diffusion and sintering (SmCo).
strategyList.outside_china: China 94% of sintered magnets. Outside: Japan and Europe, with new plants such as Neo's in Estonia.
strategyList.cost: Neo (Estonia): over EUR 100 m for 2,000 t/yr, ~EUR 250 m to reach 5,000 t/yr. India's scheme: Rs 7,280 crore for 6,000 t/yr.
strategyList.india_base: IREL's 3 t/yr SmCo plant (Vizag); 20 bids for the magnet scheme (Aug 2026); DMRL and BARC know-how.
strategyList.gap: Scale; equipment; Dy/Tb-saving diffusion; qualification with motor makers.

strategyList.name: Mineral-sands separation
strategyList.what: Gravity, magnetic and electrostatic separation of beach sand into ilmenite, rutile, zircon, monazite and sillimanite.
strategyList.india_base: IREL and KMML (KMML separates ilmenite, rutile, leucoxene, monazite and sillimanite); ~2.6% of world ilmenite.

strategyList.name: Recycling (batteries, magnets, catalysts, PV)
strategyList.what: Shredding and hydrometallurgy of black mass; magnet recovery; spent-catalyst leaching; PV-panel recovery.
strategyList.outside_china: Battery recycling: China has over three-quarters of pre-treatment and 90% of material-recovery capacity; Europe, Japan, Korea and the US smaller.
strategyList.cost: India's scheme expects ~Rs 8,000 crore for 270+ kt/yr of capacity (~Rs 30 crore per kt/yr), yielding ~40 kt/yr of critical minerals.
strategyList.india_base: Lohum, Rubamin, the Bhopal magnet facility, CSIR-NML; Rs 1,500 crore incentive scheme (2025).

chemistryList.name: Fluorochemicals and HF
chemistryList.who: GFCL (India's largest integrated fluoropolymer maker; fluorspar mine in Morocco); Navin Fluorine (AHF project at Dahej).
chemistryList.carries_over_to: LiPF6 electrolyte salt; HF purification of graphite; rare-earth fluorides for metal making; etching chemicals for gallium and silicon devices.
chemistryList.fit: Direct for LiPF6; adjacent for the rest
chemistryList.summary: Fluorine chemistry is a shared industrial foundation for battery salts, selected mineral-purification routes and electronic chemicals. India's existing HF plants provide a starting point, but each application needs its own process, purity controls and customer qualification.

links.how: Rare-earth fluorides are intermediates or bath components in selected metal-making routes. Existing fluorination skills could support their preparation after individual rare earths have been separated. Nd, Pr, Dy and Tb connect particularly to magnets; Gd's inclusion is a chemical adjacency, not a claim that it has identical demand or processing economics.

chemistryList.name: Liquid-liquid extraction and purification (pharma, agrochemicals)
chemistryList.who: India's drug industry (third largest by volume); API makers; Sudeep Pharma.
chemistryList.carries_over_to: Solvent-extraction cascades for rare earths and purified phosphoric acid; high-purity salts.
chemistryList.summary: A reusable separation skill: move selected molecules or metal ions between two liquids, then recover a purified product. India has chemical equipment suppliers and actual mineral-separation operators; transferring pharmaceutical experience to a new mineral still requires a qualified flowsheet.

links.how: Separates rare earths from mixed chloride feeds into distinct products. IREL lists Nd-Pr, Sm, Gd and Y outputs, although mixed Nd-Pr is not independently separated Nd and Pr. Required purity depends on the intended customer.
links.fit: Direct mineral-separation base; pharma contribution is adjacent

chemistryList.name: Hydrometallurgy and process R&D
chemistryList.carries_over_to: Tellurium from slime; nickel from overburden; magnet and battery recycling; REE separation flowsheets.
chemistryList.summary: Hydrometallurgy dissolves and separates elements into useful products. India has process-development experience, pilot facilities and some industrial transfers. That foundation can support several mineral chains; each feed still needs its own validated flowsheet and commercial case.

links.how: IREL’s historical product literature identifies Nd–Pr combined material and Sm, Gd and Y compounds. NML lists developed neodymium recovery from hard-drive waste. These are specific product precedents, not independent separation of every rare earth.
links.fit: Commercial foundation for listed products, with further development by route
